h1: ETIAS for UK travellers: what to expect when it launches
intro: ETIAS for UK travellers is the EU’s new online travel authorisation, and it’s expected to start in the last quarter of 2026. It isn’t open yet, so nobody can apply today. Here’s what we know about the fee, who needs it, how it fits with the new Entry/Exit System, and how to avoid the scam websites already selling it.

sections.heading: What is ETIAS?
sections.text:
ETIAS stands for the European Travel Information and Authorisation System. It’s a pre-travel check for people who don’t need a visa to visit Europe, including British passport holders. You fill in a short online form before you travel, pay a fee, and get an approval linked to your passport.

It isn’t a visa. It works in a similar way to the US ESTA or the UK’s own ETA. You’ll still go through passport control and border officers can still refuse entry.

sections.heading: When does ETIAS start?
sections.text:
The EU has said ETIAS will start operating in the last quarter of 2026, but it hasn’t yet announced an exact opening date. When it does launch, there’s expected to be a transition period of several months before an approval becomes compulsory.

Until the EU confirms the date, you don’t need to do anything. Keep an eye on the official [ETIAS website](https://travel-europe.europa.eu/etias_en) or on our [visa news](/news/) page, where we’ll post the date as soon as it’s confirmed.

sections.heading: ETIAS for UK travellers: the key facts
sections.text:
- Fee: €20 per application. Under-18s and people over 70 don’t pay.
- Validity: 3 years, or until your passport expires if that’s sooner. Renew your passport and you’ll need a new ETIAS.
- Trips covered: short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, for holidays, family visits and business meetings.
- Countries: the Schengen countries plus Cyprus, 30 European countries in total.
- Decision time: most applications are expected to be approved within minutes, though some may take a few days if more checks are needed.

sections.heading: How ETIAS works with the Entry/Exit System
sections.text:
ETIAS is the second part of the EU’s new border systems. The first, the Entry/Exit System (EES), has been fully running since 10 April 2026. EES replaces passport stamps with a digital record: the first time you cross the border you give your fingerprints and a photo, and each later crossing is recorded automatically.

EES is free and you don’t apply for it in advance. ETIAS is the part you’ll apply and pay for online before you travel.

sections.heading: Who doesn’t need ETIAS?
sections.text:
- People who need a Schengen visa. If you live in the UK on a non-visa-exempt passport, for example an Indian, Pakistani, Nigerian or Chinese passport, you’ll still need a [Schengen visa](/schengen-visa-application/) rather than ETIAS.
- Citizens of EU countries and people with EU residence rights, such as holders of a residence card or a Withdrawal Agreement document.
- Irish citizens.

sections.heading: Watch out for ETIAS scams
sections.text: Several websites already claim to sell ETIAS, often at many times the real fee. You can’t apply for ETIAS yet. When it opens, the only official place to apply will be the EU’s ETIAS website or app. Never pay a site that asks for an ETIAS or EES fee before the EU has launched the scheme.

sections.heading: How we can help
sections.text: If you hold a passport that needs a Schengen visa, we can prepare your application, book your appointment and check your documents. Read about our [Schengen visa service](/schengen-visa-application/) or call our Manchester office.

faqs.q: Do UK citizens need ETIAS now?
faqs.a: No. ETIAS hasn’t launched yet. You can travel to Europe as you do now, and you’ll go through the Entry/Exit System checks at the border.
€20 per person. Under-18s and people over 70 are exempt from the fee.

faqs.q: Will I need ETIAS for a short holiday?
faqs.a: Yes, once it becomes compulsory. It covers all short stays of up to 90 days, however short the trip.

faqs.q: Is ETIAS the same as a Schengen visa?
faqs.a: No. ETIAS is a travel authorisation for visa-free nationalities such as British citizens. People who need a visa must still apply for a Schengen visa.

faqs.q: Will ETIAS for UK travellers apply to children?
faqs.a: Yes, every traveller needs their own ETIAS, including children. Under-18s don’t pay the fee, but a parent or guardian completes the form for them.
